apex/apex-security-patterns.topic: SOQL/SOSL/DML/Database operations default to user mode in Apex
apex/apex-security-patterns.why_new: In Summer '26 (API 67.0), the default access mode for Apex database operations flipped from system mode to user mode. The Apex Developer Guide now states "In API version 67.0 and later, Apex runs in user context by default, meaning that the current user's permissions and field-level security (FLS) are enforced during code execution" and "In API version 66.0 and earlier, system mode is the default." The change is gated on the compiled API version of the class, so existing classes keep old behaviour until their version is raised. A 2024-era corpus was written entirely against the pre-67.0 world where system mode was the default and user mode was strictly opt-in via WITH USER_MODE / AccessLevel.USER_MODE. (verified: the cited page carries all three sentences verbatim — "In API version 67.0 and later, Apex runs in user context by default...", "In API version 66.0 and earlier, system mode is the default.", and "Apex database operations run in user mode by default, which means that they apply the sharing rules, field-level security (FLS), and object permissions of the running user.")
apex/apex-security-patterns.llm_gets_this_wrong: An older model says "Apex runs in system mode by default, so FLS and object permissions are NOT enforced unless you add WITH USER_MODE, AccessLevel.USER_MODE, Security.stripInaccessible(), or manual isAccessible() checks." At API 67.0+ that is backwards: the query already enforces FLS/CRUD/sharing, and the real hazard is the opposite one — integration, batch, and system-utility code that legitimately needs elevated access now silently returns fewer rows or throws unless it explicitly opts in to WITH SYSTEM_MODE / AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE. Advice to 'add user mode for security' is now a no-op, and advice that omits the system-mode opt-in causes silent data loss when a class is recompiled at 67.0.

flow/screen-flow-radio-button-group.topic: Apex triggers always run in system mode and cannot declare sharing or access modes
flow/screen-flow-radio-button-group.why_new: Summer '26 carved triggers out of the new user-mode/with-sharing defaults via the release note "Apex Triggers Always Run in System Mode" (release-notes.rn_apex_triggers_system_mode.htm, release=262). Triggers uniformly bypass sharing rules, FLS, and object permissions of the running user, and cannot be declared with explicit sharing or access modes; the documented guidance is to delegate business logic to trigger handler classes where sharing and access mode can be set. CORRECTION to the original framing: this is NOT gated on API 67.0 — the release note says the versioned change applies to ALL API versions. The substantive change is that previously nested triggers enforced sharing rules in certain edge cases, and that inconsistency is now resolved. (verified: release note exists under the exact claimed title and ID at release=262; the no-explicit-sharing-or-access-mode rule and the handler-delegation guidance are confirmed, as is the all-API-versions scope and the removed nested-trigger edge case.)
flow/screen-flow-radio-button-group.llm_gets_this_wrong: Two errors. First, a model that has learned the new 67.0 user-mode default will over-generalize and claim triggers now enforce FLS and sharing too — they do not, at any API version. Second, an older model will assert that a trigger can carry sharing semantics itself, or that triggers inherit the calling context's sharing, and will not know that the nested-trigger edge case where sharing WAS enforced has been removed. The correct current answer is that trigger context is unconditionally system mode regardless of API version, and any user-mode enforcement must be moved into a handler class that explicitly declares it.
